summary: Prepare and qualify stricter primary-Claude ownership (real installed topology remains unverified), isolating a Claude seat's channel and hooks from nested Claude processes, and retain automatic channel-recovery attempts across brief replacement success.

replay.detail: No claim replay or projection rebuild.

schema.detail: No database schema, replicated claim format or migration changes. New controlled Claude generations retain an additive local process-generation witness alongside their existing harness ownership.

rules.detail: No claim vocabulary or admission-rule change. Existing fenced runtime actions and mailbox epochs remain in use.

compatibility.detail: The direct-parent rule is a NEW restriction compared with the old any-descendant Linux admission; a legitimate launcher shim could be falsely refused, so it must not ship enabled without accepted topology evidence. Darwin is UNQUALIFIED until its existing hosted macos-ci lane executes the real child-chain controls. Nested channels serve an unscoped MCP protocol and cannot bind a protected primary seat; nested hooks cannot publish its native-session or observation state. Nested-Claude isolation is restart-gated: it protects only wrappers started after the upgrade. Existing wrapper generations without a witness retain legacy admission until their next natural authorized restart; doctor reports those seats as unprotected, so upgrading only the daemon does NOT protect the person's currently running legacy seat and the present symptom can continue until a separately authorized natural wrapper launch. Legacy shadow decisions only describe sampled topology and never change admission or recovery. Old daemons ignore the additive witness. The automatic replacement start reason now identifies automatic recovery instead of explicit intent; mixed fleets retain the old reason text from old members.

manual.detail: No agent conduct, environment stripping, configuration or tool restrictions are required.

recovery.detail: NEW visible recovery policy: only new requests stamped with the versioned existing operation value spend this budget; adoption does not inherit prior restart attempts or their park faults, which remain visible history. Old pending automatic requests retain their existing action semantics and automatic initiator; this is not observational-only daemon adoption. Automatic success does not erase attempts. Three automatic channel-recovery restart attempts within a persisted rolling six-hour window park channel recovery with its existing owner-visible fault; explicit authorized restart or expiry reopens the budget. Parking targets only its recorded incarnation. Existing explicit restart and required deployment paths remain available. Mixed old daemons do not recognize the versioned automatic operation value and can use older completion/reason behavior; no mixed-version policy guarantee is claimed.

downtime.detail: Source qualification does not authorize interrupting an active seat or establish installed-process remediation. Kernel and synthetic controls require ordinary hosted qualification.
